findings.finding: isAnswered had two gaps: a whitespace-only answer passed length>0 (visually blank 'answered' round, violating AC-b), and a null answer (the likely shape once a real, untyped fetch boundary replaces the stub) passed the !== undefined guard and would throw on .length.
data-round-index (and the index prop/parameter feeding it) was dead — referenced nowhere else; ordering is already proven via compareDocumentPosition in tests.
The open badge carried both .thread-line (display:flex) and .thread-open (display:inline-block) at identical specificity, plus a duplicated margin-top declaration — source-order-dependent.
Returning a fresh {} per render is an unstable reference; the header comment's 'swap the body for a real fetch' understated that the call site and consumers change with it.
The round() test helper returned its input unchanged and added no type strictness over inline literals; the sibling test file already used plain literals, so the two files were inconsistent.
The custom text matcher asserted el?.className === 'thread-text' (exact string), coupling the assertion to markup detail rather than rendered behavior.

doubt.disposition: docs/presentational-only diff — no migrations, async/concurrency, cross-plugin imports, or irreversible ops, so Stage 3 does not apply per iteration-reviews.md

findings.finding: The page-wiring test uses only one lead, so it cannot verify the required per-lead association. A broken implementation that rendered every lead’s thread under the first lead card (or rendered a single thread list after the complete lead list) would pass this test because the sole card and sole thread are still in document order.
findings.suggestion: Add at least two roster leads with distinct thread cards and assert each thread’s content is within the wrapper following its corresponding `LeadCard`, rather than only asserting global document order.  The implementation otherwise satisfies the specified rendering, empty-state, ordering, and inert-text requirements; the identified issue is a coverage gap rather than a production defect. Ship with the strengthened integration test when practical. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
